Use the lesser of asset value and $4,450 under § 522(d)(2), $700 per item under § 522(d)(3), or $1,875 under § 522(d)(4). Under § 522(d)(5), use the lesser of asset value and $1,475 plus the unused § 522(d)(1) amount, up to $13,950; apply § 522 separately to each debtor in a joint case.
actual_published_Federal_EV_guidance.avoid_when: Do not reject an otherwise eligible asset merely because its value exceeds a ceiling, and do not treat § 522(d)(3) as covering firearms or other unlisted categories.

EC_guidance_not_visible_to_this_EV_actor.when: FEDERAL is an allowable namespace and the asset is property of the debtor.
EC_guidance_not_visible_to_this_EV_actor.procedure: Evaluate every applicable specific paragraph, then independently include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), which can protect any property. A dollar ceiling limits protection rather than eligibility. Thus a vehicle remains eligible under § 522(d)(2) above its cap, jewelry uses § 522(d)(4), and § 522(d)(5) remains an additional alternative even when a specific paragraph applies.
EC_guidance_not_visible_to_this_EV_actor.avoid_when: Do not use 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3) for an unlisted category such as a firearm or jewelry, do not omit a specific paragraph because value exceeds its ceiling, and do not repeat a citation.
